transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, it's a burning when I pass water, and I'm needing to go much more often than usual. It's been going on a little while now and it's getting tiresome.
When did you first notice it?
Oh, it's been about two weeks now.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
I can't say I've noticed anything in particular that makes a difference, no. It's just there, mostly when I'm passing water.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
It's a stinging, burning sort of feeling when I go — I'd say about a 5 out of 10. Uncomfortable, but I'm managing.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
Just down below, when the water comes out. No, it doesn't spread anywhere — I've not had any back or side pain.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
I'd put it at about a 5. Uncomfortable but manageable, really.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?

The stinging is really just when I'm passing water. But the needing to go is fairly constant — I'm going about every hour during the day, and I'm up three or four times at night, when usually it's only once.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?

The water looks cloudy and smells stronger than usual. I've not seen any blood, though. And I've not had a fever, shivers, or any sickness — my niece hasn't noticed me being confused or anything like that.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?

Yes, I have an underactive thyroid, and I take a tablet for that. And I've got thin bones — I take something once a week for those. I had a water infection about a year ago too, but that cleared up with antibiotics.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?

I take a levothyroxine tablet, 75 micrograms, each morning for my thyroid. Then once a week I take an alendronic acid tablet, 70 mg, for my thin bones. And I use a vaginal cream from the hospital twice a week — I'm afraid I can't remember the name of it.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
Yes, I'm allergic to trimethoprim — it gave me an itchy rash.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
Well, I've stopped going to the residents' coffee morning. I'm worried I won't make it to the toilet in time.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
I do think it's another water infection, like the one I had last year. I'm hoping I can get some antibiotics before the weekend comes.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
